questions.question: Trailers with low clearance underneath may be hard to drive:
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings can be difficult to cross with a trailer that has low clearance underneath. Low trailers and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers have the most trouble crossing raised railroad crossings.

questions.question: After you connect the air lines to the trailer during coupling, you should:
questions.explanation: Following the correct steps to couple and uncouple trailers is critical for safe operation. After connecting the air lines to the trailer during coupling, supply air to the trailer.

questions.question: When entering or crossing traffic in a combination vehicle, it is especially important to:

options.text: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to make room for your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than regular vehicles. When entering or crossing traffic, make sure you have a large enough gap to do so safely.

questions.question: Trailers built before 1975:

options.text: Do not have to have spring brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not have to have spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not have to have spring brakes. When parking a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to keep the trailer from rolling.

questions.question: Test the tractor protection valve by:

options.text: Removing the parking brake control knob.
Releasing air with the brake pedal.
Releasing air with the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Releasing air with the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Test the tractor protection valve by letting the air supply charge fully, turning off the engine, then pressing the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to its emergency position when air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: If an air supply control is in its "emergency" position:

options.text: The trailer emergency brakes will apply.
The air supply to the trailer will increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes will apply.
questions.explanation: Older vehicles may have tractor protection controls that use levers instead of knobs. When an air supply control is in the "emergency" position, the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes apply.

questions.question: Avoid making sudden lane changes by:

options.text: Using your horn to get other drivers to move.
Only driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Sudden lane changes are dangerous when driving a combination vehicle. Look ahead at the road to see obstacles that may require you to change lanes.

questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer, the tractor should be:

options.text: Directly in front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: When backing up to couple a trailer, position the tractor directly in front of the trailer. Backing at an angle can cause the trailer to move and break the landing gear.

questions.question: In a sudden turn, the ____ trailer is most likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Make turns slowly and smoothly. Quick turns while pulling trailers are dangerous and increase the risk of the last trailer rolling over.

questions.question: In a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve will pop out when air pressure drops to between:
questions.explanation: In vehicles with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve pops out when air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi. When the valve pops out, it closes and stops air from flowing.

questions.question: When should you look into the back of the fifth wheel?

options.text: If your vehicle begins to skid.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling, go under the trailer and look into the back of the fifth wheel. Check that the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: What should you do before starting a trip?

options.text: Leave the service line valve open.

questions.explanation: Before a trip, open the rear emergency and service line shut-off valves. Listen for escaping air to confirm all air brakes work. Then close both shut-off valves before you start driving.

questions.question: When uncoupling a trailer, the landing gear should be:
questions.explanation: Always raise the landing gear completely before driving. When uncoupling, lower the landing gear until it firmly touches the ground. If the trailer is loaded, crank it a few more times to remove weight from the trailer.

questions.question: Low underneath clearance on trailers can be a problem when crossing:
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are difficult when pulling a trailer with low underneath clearance. Low-slung units and single-axle tractors with long trailers have special trouble crossing raised railroad crossings.

questions.question: What do you test by pulling out the trailer air supply control?
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before each trip. First, make sure the trailer rolls freely. Then pull out the trailer air supply control or set it to emergency. Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: How do you test the trailer service brakes?

options.text: Move forward slowly and apply brakes with the brake pedal.
Move backward slowly and apply brakes with the hand control.
Move forward slowly and apply brakes with the hand control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward slowly and apply brakes with the hand control.
questions.explanation: First, check that the air pressure is normal and release the parking brake. Then move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control. If the trailer service brakes work properly, you will feel them activate.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too fast. To avoid rolling over, drive slowly on ramps and corners. Avoid making quick lane changes when towing trailers.

questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System will activate.
The service air line will activate.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If pressure is lost in the emergency line, the trailer emergency brakes will activate automatically.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, how should trailers be positioned?

options.text: Cargo weight must be evenly distributed between all trailers.
The heaviest trailer should be directly behind the cab.
The heaviest trailer should be in the rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The heaviest trailer should be directly behind the cab.
questions.explanation: Position the heaviest trailer closest to the tractor. Place the lightest trailer in the rear.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, how should you press the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: When using Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), apply the brakes the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
